name: 1847 Great Aurora

phenomena.details: Major geomagnetic storm during the ascending phase of Solar Cycle 9; widespread aurora reports.

impacts.description: Brilliant aurora observed across Europe and North America at low latitudes, widely reported in newspapers and scientific correspondence of the era.
Early telegraph systems experienced disturbances, though the telegraph network was still in its infancy during this period.

papers.title: LXI. On the Aurora Borealis, as it was seen on Sunday evening, October 24, 1847, at Blackheath
papers.journal: The London, Edinburgh, and Dublin Philosophical Magazine and Journal of Science
papers.keyFinding: Contemporary account by James Glaisher of the great aurora of 24 October 1847 as observed from Greenwich, describing its extent and colour.

summary: The October 1847 great aurora, occurring during the ascending phase of Solar Cycle 9 in the early era of systematic solar observations, produced widespread aurora across Europe and North America at low latitudes.
description: In late October 1847, a major geomagnetic storm produced aurora visible across much of Europe and North America. This event occurred during Solar Cycle 9, when systematic sunspot observation programmes established by Heinrich Schwabe were providing the first continuous records of solar activity. The storm affected early telegraph systems, though the network was still limited compared to its extent at the time of the 1859 Carrington Event. The event demonstrates that intense space weather was occurring well before the Carrington Event, during a period when instrumentation was just beginning to capture solar-terrestrial connections.
